title: Staged Sweep Enactor for cost Optimize recommendations with canary simulations and operator escalation
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Build an enactor service (Staged Sweep) that can safely apply vetted batching and KV-cache recommendations from Optimize to customer routes in controlled waves. The enactor must support dry-run canary simulations (shadow traffic + telemetry validation), explicit operator escalation for ambiguous regressions, automated rollback hooks, per-customer policy scoping, and an approvals integration with Console. Goals: (1) reduce per-token unit cost by automatically applying low-risk suggestions, (2) keep latency and quality regressions below SLO thresholds, (3) provide clear operator controls and auditability.
acceptance_criteria: Enactor can pull approved suggestions from Optimize and schedule a staged sweep with configurable wave sizes and pause checkpoints
Canary simulation mode that runs shadowed requests through candidate configs and records latency/cost/quality deltas in Console for X minutes
Automatic gating rules: abort if latency P95 increases > 10% or generation failure rate rises above 0.5% over canary window
Operator dashboard shows per-wave telemetry, diffs, and a single-click rollback that restores previous config and annotates audit log
Audit trail entry for every applied change including suggestion id, model, route, applied_by (service/actor), and commit sha
Integrates with approvals matrix: enactor will not apply suggestions for 'enterprise' customers without explicit approval flag
End-to-end e2e tests in CI that simulate traffic and verify rollback path works under injected errors
design_decisions: Use shadowed traffic for canary simulations rather than synthetic replays to capture real distribution of tokens and sequence lengths
Wave sizes will be percent-based (e.g., 1%, 5%, 25%) and configurable per-customer class to respect Dedicated/Private customers
Gating thresholds default conservative; exposed to Console for product teams to tune per-workload
Persist applied configs in ConfigStore with versioned metadata; use existing rollout-controller to coordinate waves rather than building a new scheduler
Store telemetry snapshots in a time-series namespace so diffs are reproducible for postmortems
tradeoffs_and_risks: Shadowing adds extra load: we will limit canary window and sampling rate to avoid capacity impact
Synthetic replay would be cheaper but is less accurate for KV-cache hit distributions and batching behavior
Stricter default gates reduce cost savings but minimize customer impact; ops can relax gates after validation
Rollback latency vs data consistency: quick rollback may leave partial KV-cache states; document eventual consistency implications in runbook
implementation_plan: Phase 1: API + CRD - create Enactor API, scheduling CRD, and ConfigStore hooks (2 sprints)
Phase 2: Canary Simulation - implement shadowing pipeline and telemetry collectors; build gating evaluator (1 sprint)
Phase 3: Operator UX - Console dashboard with per-wave metrics, approve/escalate buttons, and single-click rollback (1 sprint)
Phase 4: Security & Compliance - add audit log export and KMS signatures for applied commits (0.5 sprint)
Phase 5: E2E tests, load testing, and staging rollout (1 sprint)
Phase 6: Beta with select customers and runbook refinement (1 sprint)
Estimate total ~6 weeks of core engineering + QA
tasks: API: POST /enactor/sweeps, GET /enactor/sweeps/:id, PATCH to pause/rollback
Scheduler: integrate with rollout-controller to apply staged config changes
Shadowing pipeline: implement request copier, sidecar or service mesh hook
Telemetry: extend Console to ingest canary diffs and show cost/latency/quality charts
Gates: implement evaluator service with config-driven thresholds and alerting
Approvals: wire into approvals service; respect enterprise approval flags
Runbook: draft operator playbook for escalation and rollback procedures
E2E tests: CI flows that inject latency/error and verify abort/rollback behaviors
Load test: simulate sweep across 200 routes to measure overhead
qa_and_validation: Create a staging workload with representative model families and sequence length distribution
Run canary simulation at 0.5% traffic for 30 min and validate metrics collector
Introduce synthetic regression (increase LLM latency by 15%) and verify gate aborts
Verify rollback restores previous config and that console audit log contains traceable commit sha
Security review for audit logs and KMS signing (coordinate with Security on 2026-03-10)
Run automated hallucination/regression check on sampled outputs during canary
monitoring_and_slas: Track per-wave P95 latency, token cost delta, error/generation-failure rate, and KV-cache hit rate
Create Console alerts: gate_abort, surge_in_shadow_traffic, failed_rollback
SLO: applied changes must not cause >10% P95 latency regression or >0.5% absolute failure-rate increase for monitored routes
Retention: store canary telemetry for 90 days for audit and for model-ops comparisons
